cards.text: It's the seventh month, and the Israelites are settled in their towns. Then everybody comes to Jerusalem, and the Bible says they gather “as one man.” A whole crowd moving like ONE guy, friend, and I couldn't get six little cookie cutters to agree on a topping!

Two leaders step up: Jeshua son of Jozadak with his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel with his associates. They're ready to sacrifice burnt offerings to the God of Israel, just like it's written in the Law of Moses.

cards.question: Jeshua and Zerubbabel are ready to offer burnt offerings to the God of Israel. So what do they start building first?

cards.text: They set the altar up on its foundation, and the burnt offerings to the LORD begin, morning and evening. But something is hanging over all of it.

cards.question: The Israelites keep the morning and evening burnt offerings going, even though they ___ the people of the land.

cards.text: Scared? I bet some knees were knocking. Stopping? NOPE. The altar keeps going, and then they celebrate a feast, just like it's written.

cards.question: The Israelites celebrate a feast, just like it's written. Which feast is it?
During the Feast of Tabernacles, the Israelites offer burnt offerings every day, following the number prescribed for each day.

cards.text: After that, the altar gets a FULL schedule: the regular burnt offerings, the New Moons, all the appointed sacred feasts of the LORD, plus every freewill offering people bring. That altar's got a busier calendar than my ovens, and friend, my ovens are BUSY.

cards.question: When the Israelites start offering burnt offerings on the first day of the seventh month, the foundation of the temple of the LORD has already been laid.

cards.text: Now it's time to build. They pay the masons and carpenters, and they send food, drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon.

cards.question: The cedar logs from Lebanon make their way to Joppa by ___.

cards.text: Trees. On a BOAT. Friend, I get antsy waiting on one little package, and these folks are waiting on a whole forest!

cards.question: This whole cedar shipment happens with the go-ahead of Cyrus, king of Persia.

cards.text: In the second month of the second year after they arrived at the house of God in Jerusalem, the work begins. Zerubbabel, Jeshua, the priests, the Levites and everyone back from captivity: all hands on deck!

cards.question: The work on the house of the LORD needs supervisors. Who do Zerubbabel and Jeshua appoint?

answers.text: Levites twenty years old and up
Builders hired from Tyre and Sidon

cards.text: So Levite families team up to oversee the workers: Jeshua's family, Kadmiel's family and the sons of Henadad. Nothing makes you lay a stone straighter than a supervisor standing right behind you!
And then it happens: the builders lay the foundation of the temple of the LORD. A FOUNDATION, friend, an actual FOUNDATION!

cards.question: To praise the LORD, the priests take their positions with ___, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, come with ___.
The priests and Levites praise the LORD the way ___ king of Israel had prescribed.

cards.text: They sing back and forth with praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “For He is good; for His loving devotion to Israel endures forever.”

cards.question: Then all the people give a great shout of praise to the LORD. What has them shouting?

cards.text: Now listen close, friend. Not every sound in that crowd is a cheer.

cards.question: Some in the crowd weep loudly when they see the foundation of this temple. Who are they?

answers.text: Older leaders who had seen the first temple
Young workers who had hauled the cedar
Persian officials who had come along

cards.question: Everyone at the foundation weeps loudly.

cards.text: Some weeping, some shouting, same foundation. I know that one, friend: every time somebody opened that junk drawer I spent years in, I didn't know whether to cheer or cry, so I just held my breath and did NEITHER!

cards.question: With the weeping and the shouting going on at once, what can't the people do?

answers.text: Tell the shouts of joy from the weeping
Hear the trumpets over all the crowd
Finish singing the song they started

cards.question: The sound of that crowd is heard from far away.

cards.text: Joy and tears all mixed together, loud enough to carry. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because the house of the LORD isn't built yet, and this story's not done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "as one man.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This is passage 2 of 5 and starts in the middle of the story, but the opening card never says who these Israelites are: exiles back from captivity, about to restore worship in Jerusalem. The baker first hears they came back from captivity in stop 2, card 5.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke invents a past moment for his kids: 'I couldn't get six little cookie cutters to agree on a topping.' This adds something new to his backstory. It also clashes with it. In the Millers' kitchen the kids were cutters with no toppings. He named the toppings after them later, in the Dorinverse, after they were gone.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke ('Trees. On a BOAT...'). It tells nothing new from Ezra 3:7, and the shipment by sea was already covered on cards 1 and 2. The joke should ride along on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Verse 9's Jeshua is a Levite, not Jeshua son of Jozadak the priest from card 2 and card 5. The card says 'Jeshua's family' and never says who he is, so the baker will think this is the same Jeshua.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 14's question already says 'Some in the crowd weep loudly,' which gives away that not everyone weeps. That makes card 15 ('Everyone at the foundation weeps loudly') answered before it is asked. Asking what the others do (they shout joyfully, 3:12) would test the verse instead.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card starts by recapping verse 12 ('Some weeping, some shouting, same foundation'), which cards 13 through 15 already covered. After that it is only a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

The wrong answer 'Hear the trumpets over all the crowd' is arguable. Verse 13 says the people were making so much noise, and the text never says the trumpets could still be heard, so a baker could argue it is right.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
